question.value: Reveal the distributions of HCN and HCO+ J=3-2 emission in local U/LIRGs and investigate whether and how their line ratios relate to galaxy properties, AGN strength, excitation conditions, and outflows/inflows.

evidence.quote: We aim to reveal the distributions of HCN and HCO [+] emission in local U/LIRGs and investigate whether and how they are related to galaxy properties.

Specifically, we tackle the following questions: Can the HCN/HCO [+] line ratio by itself be used as a diagnostic tool for the AGN strength in moderate-resolution (several tens to hundreds of parsec) observations?

findings_qualitative.value: Global and resolved HCN/HCO+ line ratios show no statistically significant correlation with AGN fraction, bolometric AGN luminosity, infrared luminosity, star formation rate, or dust temperature.

evidence.quote: These line ratios appear to have no systematic trend with bolometric AGN luminosity or star formation rate.

findings_qualitative.value: In eight out of ten galaxies with known molecular outflows and/or inflows, spaxels with HCN/HCO+ above the 90th percentile form spatially and kinematically symmetric structures in ppV space (collimated bicones in two galaxies and thin spherical shells in six galaxies).

evidence.quote: In eight out of ten galaxies known to have outflows and/or inflows, we found spatially and kinematically symmetric structures of high line ratios. These structures appear as a collimated bicone in two galaxies and as a thin spherical shell in six galaxies.

findings_qualitative.value: Non-LTE RADEX modeling indicates X(HCN)/X(HCO+) >= 10 is required to achieve L'_HCN/L'_HCO+ >= 1 unless gas density exceeds 10^6 cm^-3, and electron collisions can further enhance the ratio by more than a factor of two at moderate densities (10^3-10^5 cm^-3) when X_e- = 10^-4.

evidence.quote: X HCN / X HCO [+] ≳ 10 is necessary to get L HCN [′] [/] [L] HCO [′] [+] [ ≳] [1 unless the density is very high] (≳10 [6] cm [−][3] ).

claims.experiment: Extracted global HCN and HCO+ J=3-2 line luminosities from 10x10 beam apertures and performed linear regression in log-log space against L_IR.
claims.result: Both L'_HCN and L'_HCO+ correlate strongly with L_IR (Pearson r = 0.85 and 0.90), with best-fit slopes of 0.53 ± 0.03 and 0.61 ± 0.03.

claims.hypothesis: Spatially and spectrally resolved high HCN/HCO+ line ratios trace molecular outflows and inflows in U/LIRGs.
claims.experiment: Calculated spaxel-by-spaxel (0.05'' x 0.05'' x 20 km s^-1) HCN/HCO+ ratios and visualized spaxels above the 90th percentile in 3D position-position-velocity (ppV) space.
claims.result: In 8 out of 10 galaxies with known molecular outflows and/or inflows, the >90th percentile spaxels form symmetric 3D structures: collimated bicones in 2 galaxies and thin spherical shells in 6 galaxies.
claims.finding: Spatially and spectrally resolved HCN/HCO+ line ratios in ppV space can identify outflow and inflow geometries when shock velocities are sufficiently high.

evidence.quote: In eight out of ten galaxies known to have outflows and/or inflows, we found spatially and kinematically symmetric structures of high line ratios. These structures appear as a collimated bicone in two galaxies and as a thin spherical shell in six galaxies.
These results imply that the HCN/HCO [+] line ratio can aid in identifying the outflow geometry when the shock velocity of the outflows is sufficiently high to heat the gas.

why_this_data.value: Submillimeter molecular lines (HCN and HCO+ J=3-2) are less affected by severe dust extinction in compact obscured nuclei, and the sample was restricted to two dedicated ALMA programs with homogeneous sensitivity and ~0.3'' spatial resolution to allow proper galaxy-to-galaxy and spatially/spectrally resolved comparisons.

evidence.quote: Molecular lines at (sub)millimeter wavelengths are less affected by dust extinction and thus have been explored for useful diagnostic methods.

This sample selection was done to ensure that the source properties could be compared properly by only studying sources that have HCN and HCO [+] data with similar sensitivities and spatial resolutions.

why_this_method.value: Spectrally and spatially resolved (spaxel-by-spaxel) analysis in ppV space disentangles shocked outflow/inflow components from surrounding disk gas along the line of sight; non-LTE RADEX modeling accounts for subthermal excitation and electron collisions; UCLCHEM models C-shocks in the moderately-dense gas (10^3-10^4 cm^-3) that dominates extragalactic beams.

evidence.quote: As detailed in Sect. 5.3, spectrally resolved analysis would be helpful to disentangle the nuclear region from the surrounding disk regions.

limitations_admitted.value: Inclusion of six additional galaxies at slightly larger distances breaks the sample completeness held in Paper I.

evidence.quote: Inclusion of these galaxies does not change the range of the infrared luminosity of the sample as a whole but breaks the completeness of the sample held in Paper I.

limitations_admitted.value: Mid-infrared AGN diagnostics (alpha_AGN) have limitations in heavily obscured nuclei ([Ne V] and [O IV] can be attenuated, and 6.2 um PAH EQW may overestimate AGN fraction in starbursts).

evidence.quote: We used these values as best estimates while keeping in mind the limitations of mid-infrared diagnostics when dealing with obscured nuclei.

limitations_admitted.value: Interferometric missing flux beyond the effective MRS (~3-4'') and the fixed ~3'' global aperture may systematically underestimate line fluxes in the closer LIRG sample, and single-dish data are not homogeneously available.

limitations_admitted.value: No correction was applied for line blending with neighboring CH2NH, HC3N-vib, and HCN-vib lines, which may overestimate HCN and HCO+ fluxes in galaxies with broad lines (>=300 km s^-1).

evidence.quote: For simplicity, we took into account all channels within the integration range and did not apply any correction for line blending. Hence, the values should be taken with caution, particularly for the galaxies with broad line profiles (≳300 km s [−][1] )

limitations_admitted.value: 3-sigma threshold clipping in spaxel-by-spaxel analysis ignores faint but real emission below 3-sigma.

limitations_admitted.value: Collisional rate coefficients for HCO+ with electrons at J>=3 were provisionally approximated by scaling HCN rates by the square of the dipole moment.

evidence.quote: We provisionally employed the rate coefficients for J ≥3 levels generated by scaling with µ [2] based on the rate coefficients for HCN provided by Faure et al. (2007). For a robust discussion in the future, more accurate rate coefficients for HCO [+] will be necessary.

referee_caveats_inferred: Spaxels of 0.05'' x 0.05'' within the ~0.3'' synthesized beam are strongly spatially correlated (as noted in Table 6), which affects statistical distributions of spaxel-by-spaxel ratios.
Analyzing only the single J=3-2 transition of HCN and HCO+ leaves a degeneracy between excitation (temperature/density) and abundance without multi-transition constraints.
Missing short-spacing (ACA/single-dish) data can alter spatial line ratios if HCO+ (which has a lower critical density) is more spatially extended than HCN and selectively filtered out.
